feedback: Written before this candidate races. Evidence: in iteration 0 all 60 trials went off track at progress 0.10 to 0.15, with max_error at the 0.06 m limit and 1 to 2 line-loss events per run (slalom worst at 2.0). Steering oscillation was low (0.085 to 0.142), so the failure is line loss, not jitter. For this geometry the Integrator had to scale sensor weights with x (-1.5 to +1.5) and drop kp to 2.5 so the wider span does not over-correct, and trim base_speed to 1.5. Decision rules for the next race: (1) If line_loss_events fall to 0 and max_error stays under 0.06 m, keep the span and try the forward offset change next, moving y from 0.04 toward 0.03 only if steering_oscillation rises. (2) If line loss persists on the tightest bend (slalom or s-bend) with the wide span, the sensing span is not the limit. Then test a shorter forward offset or a higher kd, not a wider span. (3) If the robot completes but completion_time is near 3 s, reduce mass further (to 0.6 kg) or raise wheel_radius to 0.035. If wheels slip on starts, keep wheel_track at 0.14 and reduce mass instead.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_size 0.016 and x span -0.03 to +0.03 at 10 mm spacing. Basis: iteration 0 lost the line 1 to 2 times per run with a 4 cm span of 12 mm sensors; if line_loss_events drop, keep this span.

If line loss persists on the tightest bend, move sensor y from 0.04 to 0.03 to reduce lag. Basis: iteration 0 steering_oscillation was low (0.085 to 0.142), so the lag fix is safe to test one change at a time.

If completion_time is near 3 s with no line loss, reduce mass from 0.7 to 0.6 kg or raise wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035. Basis: iteration 0 never finished, so speed is not yet the constraint; test this only after line loss is fixed.
